decision_table.name: Determine_MN_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file Minnesota state corporate tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in MN (office, employees, property)

condition.name: has_economic_nexus
condition.comment: Meets MN economic nexus threshold ($100K or 200 transactions)

rule.policy:
Minnesota filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
Physical presence establishes nexus for Minnesota corporate franchise tax purposes. Corporation must file Form M4 and apportion income using single-sales factor.
Reference: MN Stat. § 290.015 (Definitions - Doing Business) Reference: MN Form M4 Instructions (Filing Requirements)

Minnesota filing required due to economic nexus (post-Wayfair).
Economic nexus threshold (either condition): - $100,000 or more in gross receipts from MN sources, OR - 200 or more separate transactions with MN customers
Corporation must file Form M4 even without physical presence.
Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018) Reference: MN Revenue Notice 19-03 (Economic Nexus for Corporate Franchise Tax) Reference: MN Stat. § 290.015, subd. 1(c) (Economic Nexus)

No Minnesota nexus - no filing requirement. Any estimated payments would be refunded.
Corporation has no physical presence and does not meet economic nexus thresholds.

decision_table.name: Calculate_MN_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate Minnesota state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
Minnesota state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
ADDITIONS to federal taxable income: - Interest on U.S. government obligations (federal bonds are taxable to MN) - IRC Section 199A qualified business income deduction addback - Foreign dividend deduction addback (IRC §§ 245A, 250) - Bonus depreciation addback (if MN decouples in future years) - GILTI inclusion addback (for certain taxpayers)
SUBTRACTIONS from federal taxable income: - Interest on Minnesota municipal bonds (exempt from MN tax) - State income taxes paid (not deductible for MN purposes) - Small business income deduction (for qualifying small businesses) - Minnesota NOL deduction (80% of income limitation) - Certain dividend income from foreign operating corporations
Reference: MN Stat. § 290.01, subd. 19a (Additions) Reference: MN Stat. § 290.01, subd. 19b (Subtractions) Reference: MN Form M4 Schedule M1M (Additions and Subtractions Schedule) Reference: MN Revenue Fact Sheet on Federal Conformity Updates
No nexus - no Minnesota state adjustments calculated.

decision_table.name: Calculate_MN_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate Minnesota state corporate income tax. Applies MN 9.5% flat rate to apportioned and adjusted taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
Minnesota state corporate income tax calculation:
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to MN: × [MN Apportionment % using single-sales factor] 3. MN additions: + [Additions from Schedule M1M] 4. MN subtractions: - [Subtractions from Schedule M1M] 5. MN taxable income: = [Result] 6. MN tax rate: × 9.5% (flat rate as of 2024) 7. MN income tax: = [Tax before credits] 8. MN credits: - [Credits (R&D, jobs, etc.)] 9. MN tax liability: = [Final tax]
RATE CHANGE HISTORY: - Prior to 2024: Progressive brackets up to 9.8% - 2024 and forward: Flat 9.5% rate (simplified structure)
Reference: MN Stat. § 290.06, subd. 1 (9.5% flat rate effective for tax years beginning after December 31, 2023) Reference: MN Form M4 Instructions (Line 16 - Tax Calculation) Reference: MN Department of Revenue Notice (2024 Tax Rate Simplification)
No Minnesota nexus - no tax liability. Any estimated payments are refunded.

No Minnesota taxable income - no tax liability.
Corporation has nexus but no positive taxable income after apportionment and adjustments. This may be due to: - Operating loss for the year - Subtractions exceed apportioned income - Small business income deduction reduces income to zero
Minnesota NOL rules apply for carryforward (80% limitation similar to federal). Loss can be carried forward indefinitely to offset future MN income.
Reference: MN Stat. § 290.095 (Net Operating Loss)
